## Summary
Every SKILL.md is rewritten as a procedure the agent follows (checklists, progressive disclosure, gotchas), and the ops skills get one front door: `aaif-sync` owns the pipeline, its order and its gates, and the phase skills each document one engine. The pipeline is indexed on two axes, phase (the subject) by stage (gather, plan, execute), with triage as a human gate the runner summarises and never decides. Every engine writes its report as data beside its log, and each run ends with one page that opens on the state of the estate per subject, with the logs in a collapsed appendix. A local Slack cache is trusted for a day and can never be committed. An `Ops Notes` column that people keep and scripts only quote is installed on the intake role tabs and the Chapters List.

113 files, +11,532 / −2,976, 29 commits. Every engine still reports by default and writes only behind `--write`. Two live changes were made during this work and are recorded in the commits: the `Ops Notes` headers, and one organizer's Drive grant moved to the address recorded in `Drive Email`.

## Changesets

### 1. `refactor(skills): make every SKILL.md procedural and code-driven`
Every skill onto the agent-skills guidance. The three far over the 500-line ceiling drop to a fifth of their size, with reference material moved to `references/`.

### 2. `fix(skills): correct two claims the rewrite got wrong`

### 3. `refactor(sync): one front door, one pipeline definition, four phase skills`
`aaif-sync/scripts/sync.py` is the single definition of what runs, in what order, behind which gate. `nightly.py` wraps it. `aaif-sync-chapters` splits into chapters, organizers and slack phase skills.

### 4. `fix(sync): the gitignore guard aborted the very first run it protects`
`git check-ignore` treats a path that does not exist yet as a file; the probe carries a trailing separator.

### 5. `fix(skills): restore the tooling rule, and guard the hole that hid its loss`
`check_tooling_banner_coverage.py` fails the build when a gws-driving skill lacks the banner.

### 6–7. README flowcharts; phase skills brought up to date with the pipeline

### 8–9. Triage is a human gate: the runner reports how deep the queue is (exit 2 while rows wait) and never decides it.

### 10. `feat(sync): re-index the pipeline on two axes — phase x stage`
Seven phases, each gather then plan then execute; stage order asserted at import. The Slack audit engines become the gather steps of the phases whose questions they answer.

### 11. `feat(sync): no findings from a previous run; per-role CRM tabs`
The runner keeps no state between runs. A migration adds per-role CRM tabs.

### 12. `feat(cache): a local cache is trusted for a day, and can never be committed`
`jsoncache.MAX_AGE` is one day; `check_state_never_committed.py` asserts the ignore rules.

### 13. `fix(sync): unattended approval steps report; cache consumers read at any age`
From review. Approval-gated Slack steps run read-only under `--unattended`, the same contract `access` has, so a clean night exits 0. The activity sweep runs before its consumers, and pure consumers read the cache at any age and date the sweep instead of dropping it.

### 14. `docs(sync): describe the seven-phase pipeline the runner actually defines`

### 15. `fix(sync): an indented PARTIAL marker still classifies the step as PARTIAL`
Found by the first live run: a rate-limited Luma sweep read as DRIFT.

### 16. `feat(sync): every run ends with one HTML report, in the run directory`
The audit gathers write their pages into the run directory; the audit composer is the last step.

### 17. `feat(ops): an Ops Notes column people keep, and scripts only quote`
`install_ops_notes.py` appends the column (idempotent, `--write` gated); the intake digest and the chapter health report quote it; nothing writes or acts on it. Installed live.

### 18–19. `feat(sync): the runner records a run.json; render_report.py draws report.html` / `the run page always shows the whole pipeline`
The runner records; a separate renderer draws. Every run lists all 18 steps, not-run ones marked.

### 20–22. `feat(lib): findings` / `feat(engines): every ops engine writes its report as data with --json-out` / `feat(sync): the run page opens on the state of the estate`
One shape (`lib/aaif_events/findings.py`): summary, stat tiles, finding rows with kind, subject, detail, severity and next step. Twelve engines emit it. The page opens on tiles and ranked finding tables per subject; long lists fold; logs are in the appendix.

### 23. `docs(skills): the paged digest and the collapsed scan`
Console output, measured: the triage digest fell from ~27k to ~9.5k tokens, the clean scan from ~11k to ~1.3k.

### 24–26. Every finding says who: names through `--redact` wherever the text report prints one; a duplicate is a second organizer application, not a repeated address; an unknown Drive grant names its holder; strangers in organizer rooms are named, a few plus a count, and ops staff are never strangers.

### 27–28. `fix(sync): fail closed on gates, usage errors and the render; one definition of "wrote"` / `fix(engines): guard --json-out, name what the text report names, describe strangers honestly`
From the self-review below: an unknown gate can no longer fall through to `--write`; a usage error is FAILED, not drift; the findings file's `written` is the one definition of "wrote"; `--json-out` is gitignore-guarded everywhere; an expired token aborts the stranger lookup instead of naming the ops seed as strangers; stale docstrings restated; integration and write-gate tests added.

## Test Plan

- [x] All 46 `skills/*/scripts/test_*.py` and `skills/*/migrations/test_*.py` pass
- [x] `pre-commit run --all-files` (23 hooks) and every `scripts/check_*.py` guard pass
- [x] `claude plugin validate .`
- [x] Triggering evals: the front door fires for a whole-estate request and no phase skill fires (2/2 after the description change); the write-gate case still fires `aaif-sync-chapters`
- [x] Three full report-mode runs against the live estate (18 steps, no failures, nothing written), one applied write of the open-gated steps (`resources`, `crm`) verified in sync afterwards, and a live preflight run on the final code
- [x] Self-review: six agents, 29 findings, all fixed (see the two review comments)
